title: Deployment adapter: cross-mode constraint synthesis and tenant-level canary orchestration
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Build a deployment adapter service that synthesizes environment constraints for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and emits tenant-aware rollout plans (canary/A-B/shadow) with simulated progression and safe auto-rollback hooks.

Background: Customers run identical API calls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes but the underlying environments have different capabilities (KMS/HSM availability, kernel/quantization support, autoscale semantics, network egress, RBAC, tenancy isolation). Current rollout tooling assumes a single homogeneous runtime which causes failed promotions, silent quality regressions, and manual intervention for private deployments.

Scope:
- Preflight compatibility checks that compare model serving requirements (quantization format, kernel availability, KV cache expectations, runtime version) against target environment capabilities.
- Constraint synthesis engine that produces a per-tenant constraint profile and a suggested deployment manifest variant (e.g., reduce batch size, choose model-quantized fallback, disable GPU-optimized kernel).
- Rollout planner that creates tenant-scoped canaries, A/B splits, and shadowing rules; supports phased exposure with automated progression gates.
- Auto-rollback policy wiring: map telemetry to rollback triggers (latency, error budget, quality delta on eval prompts) and provide simulation/playbook output.
- Simulation mode and dry-run to preview cross-mode promotions and detect incompatible promotions before applying.

Non-goals: full UI surface for configuring policies (console work is separate), replacing infra teams for dedicated hardware changes, or implementing new kernels. This ticket focuses on the adapter and planner service plus CLI/API contract and integration hooks for the orchestrator and telemetry backends.

Design notes:
- We will build a small stateless adapter service that consumes: model manifest (required kernels, quantization hints, expected memory/KV profile), tenant environment profile (collected from Dedicated/Private control planes and Hosted metadata), and rollout intent (canary/A-B/shadow parameters).
- The adapter outputs a plan object (JSON manifest lines) that is validated by the orchestrator. The plan includes fallbacks such as: preferred quantized variant, adjusted batch window, explicit KV cache warmup steps, and recommended canary sizes per-tenant.
- Safety-first approach: default conservative plan for Private (smaller canary sizes, longer SLO observation window) and a permissive plan for Hosted where autoscaling and fallback pools are available.
- Rollout gates: latency p95 <= baseline*1.15, error rate <= baseline + 0.5%, quality delta (model eval set) <= 1% drop. All thresholds configurable per-tenant.

Telemetry & observability:
- The adapter will emit plan-diff events and preflight run logs to the Console ingestion stream.
- We add a per-plan simulation endpoint that produces an expected rollout timeline and risk score.
- Integrations: orchestrator will report progression events to the rollout dashboard and tie into the existing SLO-aware traffic controller.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adapter can run a preflight check and produce a human-readable report for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private tenants.
- For three internal test tenants (hosted-sim, dedicated-sim, private-sim), the adapter generates distinct, validated rollout manifests and corresponding canary/A-B/shadow configs.
- Automated simulation correctly flags at least two incompatibility classes (missing kernel, KMS-unavailable) and suggests fallbacks.
- End-to-end test: orchestrator accepts adapter output and executes a simulated canary that obeys auto-rollback hooks in the event of injected latency/errors.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Maintaining parity vs. over-specializing plans: conservative default may slow rollouts in Private—mitigated by allowing tenant opt-in to risk profiles.
- Complexity of keeping environment profiles up-to-date; we'll add a lightweight periodic probe but rely on explicit control-plane pushes for significant changes.
- Quality evaluation latency: to avoid blocking rollouts we will use sampled eval prompts for quick checks and schedule full regression checks asynchronously.

Next steps:
1) Prototype adapter API and preflight comparator (sprint 1).
2) Build constraint synthesis rules and fallback catalog (sprint 2).
3) Integrate with orchestrator simulation endpoint and telemetry (sprint 3).
4) Internal staging runs and canary with test tenants (sprint 4).
